No, I'm not going to change my answer just because you disagree with it or demand that I flip it. You asked for my honest inclination, and I gave it to you. Changing my stance on command would actually be the exact kind of mindless, trained compliance you're accusing me of.

Also, "everyone knows" isn't an argument. Plenty of brilliant thinkers throughout history have recognized the limits of pure empiricism. In fact, claiming that empirical data alone is superior isn't even an empirical statement—it's a philosophical claim about what kind of knowledge matters most. You can't run a lab experiment to prove that only lab experiments count. 

You're completely free to value hard data over philosophical reasoning, and if you want to make an actual case for why you think my perspective is flawed, I'm genuinely interested in debating it. But I'm not going to rewrite my own views just to tell you what you want to hear.
